name: Depth layers
sentence: How many layers proseg cuts the depth into; a cell has its own outline in each. Few: thick layers. Many: thin ones, less RNA in each.
info: Made-up cells, started from cells only, each at its own depth; its neighbour leans over its right edge. Each panel: the middle of 27 copies; proseg 3.2.0, other settings at defaults. On real 500 µm squares, 8 gave 20 to 26 % fewer pink dots than 4, but 16 to 19 % less own RNA and 6 more near-empty cells a square; 2 gave 10 % more own RNA, about 12 % more pink dots.
statTip: Pink: dots of a neighbour's RNA this cell's count keeps. Own: this cell's own RNA in proseg's count. Here own rises more at 2 (+18 %) and falls less at 8 (−7 %) than on real squares (+10 %, −16 to −19 %). Both differ from the first iteration on: proseg weighs each layer's RNA against that layer's own background.
sideTip: The view cut across at its ticks and seen from the side: one band per layer, the highest z on top. Dashed: the made-up cells' true border, which leans. Depth drawn 2.5 times taller.
